applicability: any two-digit integer n in [10, 99]. Write n = 10a + b with a in {1,...,9} and b in {0,...,9}. Then n * 11 = 100*a + 10*(a + b) + b. When a + b < 10 the decimal digits of the answer are simply a, a+b, b (the 'drop the digit sum between the digits' shortcut). When a + b >= 10 a carry is required: the answer's digits are (a + 1), (a + b - 10), b, a four-digit number where the '1' carries into the hundreds. The full rule (with carry) is exact for every n in [10, 99] and the Verifier can confirm it exhaustively over the 90-value domain.
carry_case: any two-digit n whose digits sum to 10 or more — e.g. 92 (9 + 2 = 11). The simplified 'drop the sum between the digits' form would write 9 (11) 2, which is not a decimal number; you must carry the 1 into the hundreds place, giving 9+1 | 1 | 2 = 1012. The full carry set is exactly the 45 numbers whose digit sum is >= 10, i.e. {19, 28, 29, 37, 38, 39, 46, 47, 48, 49, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59, 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89, 91, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 97, 98, 99}.

operand_draw.construction: operand_a = drawn_value = 92; operand_b = 11 (fixed by the method being taught).
operand_draw.construction_note: The sampler draws one two-digit integer uniformly from [10, 99]; the second factor is 11 by definition of the technique. The declared range [10, 99] is exactly the method's applicability domain, so no mathematical property of the draw is being encoded through a filter — the min_digits/max_digits filter is purely rendering (both bounds already lie in the two-digit band, so it is redundant but harmless, kept for explicit intent). The draw produced 92, which happens to be a carry case (digits sum to 11). Per section 3.4 the resolution is to leave the draw alone and let the method embrace the case: the taught rule includes the carry step, so 92 fully 'suits the method'. The carry-visible worked example is a pedagogical strength here, not a mismatch.

candidates.verdict: different concept — squaring vs multiplication by a fixed factor. A viewer who watched the squaring lesson would learn a genuinely new mechanism here (digit-split + sum-between with carry, not tens-times-next + append-25).
